value.rationale: The natural first asymmetric (2,3) factor-weight slice at the first unbounded target weight four is classified globally, with five explicit unbounded families and no sporadic solutions. Kaneko–Stoll asks to characterize fixed (k,ell,m) products and leaves this boundary outside its ell,m>=3 bound; the classification resolves the exact structural carry regimes beyond a finite exercise, without pretending to solve higher-weight cases. The existence of unbounded solutions at fixed (ell,m)=(2,3) demonstrates sharp necessity of excluding input weight two from Kaneko–Stoll Theorem 2.4; this is a structural boundary not just an isolated finite count.
